title: The Bacteria That Moved Into Your Cells

lines.text: Every step you take is powered by bacteria. Well, former bacteria.
Dive into your leg, into a muscle cell, and there they are: thousands of mitochondria.
Roughly two billion years ago, a bigger cell swallowed a bacterium. But it wasn't digested. It moved in.
The guest got shelter and food. The host got energy. Lots of it.
The proof: mitochondria still carry their own DNA, wear a double wall, and split in two, just like bacteria.
Today they turn food and oxygen into ATP, your cells' fuel. You recycle about your own body weight of it every single day.
And every one of yours came from your mother. Thanks, Mom.
So every step you take runs on a deal made about two billion years ago.
